notes: All 9 exams (7 required + both optional items: a-levels-music and ib-visual-arts) were researched on 2026-11-17 from live sources; every topic line below was extracted from a source actually fetched in this pass (official PDF/page or a mirror marked as such). No URL was invented: unreachable official URLs appear as sources only where they were discovered on pages that were fetched (upsc.gov.in homepage, Cambridge subject page) or via the one working search route.

Sandbox network constraints, recorded honestly: this environment had no usable general search engine (Google 429, Bing serving unrelated junk, DuckDuckGo/Brave/Startpage/searx.be bot-blocked); the only working search was the SearXNG instance search.inetol.net rendered in a headless browser, which is how the madeeasy mirror of the UPSC ESE notice and the NID/IB mirror pages were located. Direct curl fetches worked for ugcnetonline.in, uceed.iitb.ac.in, cbseacademic.nic.in, cambridgeinternational.org, admissions.nid.edu (curl needed -k due to a sandbox CA issue) and madeeasy.in.

UGC NET subject syllabi (Performing Arts code 65, Visual Art code 79, Music code 16) are the official UGC NET Bureau syllabus PDFs ('NTA_All_R_Syllabus') served from the UGC NET portal ugcnetonline.in via its syllabus index page; the index page itself was fetched to discover the exact PDF paths.

ugc-net-performing-arts: the syllabus states Units 1-5 are common to Dance and Drama/Theatre, while Units 6-10 exist twice - once for DANCE and once for DRAMA/THEATRE - so both sets are recorded with 'Dance:' and 'Drama/Theatre:' prefixes to keep the lines distinct.

ugc-net-music: the syllabus states Units I-IV are common to all in music and Units V-X are subject-specific; the four subject-specific blocks are Hindustani (Vocal, Instrumental & Musicology), Karnataka, Percussion and Rabindra Sangeet. Hindustani and Karnataka Units V-X are recorded one line per unit; Percussion and Rabindra Sangeet are recorded as two condensed blocks (their unit titles are listed within each line) to keep the ledger at unit/topic-area granularity.
ugc-net-visual-arts: 10 common units plus five electives exactly as stated (Art History; Drawing and Painting; Applied Art; Printmaking (Graphic Art); Sculpture).

nata: nata.in sits behind a bot challenge that blocked both curl and the headless browser (homepage and brochure PDF alike), so the official brochure PDF could not be fetched from this sandbox; the test areas below were taken from the PhysicsWallah (pw.live) mirror of the official CoA brochure structure (Part A Drawing & Composition 80 marks; Part B Aptitude & Mathematics 120 marks, MCQ+NCQ). The official brochure URL is still listed as a source because it was discovered via the working search instance, with this caveat in the notes.
uceed: topic lines are verbatim from the official UCEED 2027 syllabus page at IIT Bombay (Part-A: seven topics; Part-B: two topics).

nid-dat: the official NID Admissions Handbook 2027-28 (B.Des/5.5-year integrated pathway, published 10 September 2026) states the two-stage DAT structure (DAT Prelims pen-and-paper test with questions that 'may involve text and visuals'; DAT Mains consisting of a Studio Sensitivity Test and an In-Person Sensitivity Test) but publishes NO topic list; the typical content areas of recent Prelims papers are recorded from the AglaSem mirror and are marked as such in the lines.

cbse-fine-arts: the official Classes XI-XII Fine Arts curriculum document (subject codes 049-052, 2026-27) covers four subjects (Painting, Graphics, Sculpture, Applied Art/Commercial Art) whose THEORY syllabus is common across all four; theory units are recorded once, and each subject's distinct practical units are recorded per subject, per class where they differ.

a-levels-music: Cambridge International AS & A Level Music 9483, current syllabus for exams in 2027 and 2028 (version 4) from the official syllabus PDF; the five assessment components are recorded as the syllabus states them (A Level candidates take Paper 1, Component 2 and two of Components 3/4/5).

ib-visual-arts: chosen as the syllabus-stable IB arts subject (three-component portfolio structure unchanged since first assessment 2017). ibo.org is Cloudflare-blocked (403) for both curl and headless browser, so the structure was taken from two independent mirrors (ibcourses.net, fetched in full; RevisionDojo, fetched in full and agreeing on the three components and SL/HL split), following the same approach the physics ledger used for IB Physics.
Granularity: unit/topic-area level as each syllabus states it; sub-lines after an em-dash condense the syllabus's own sub-bullets and are not invented.

sources.nature: official (syllabus index page that lists the PDF links)

topics: Unit I: Fundamentals of visual art (line, shape, form, space, colour, texture, tonal values, perspective, design; visual principles of composition such as proportion, unity, harmony, rhythm, contrast, balance, foreshortening and emphasis)
Unit II: Various forms of visual arts and their inter-relationship with other modes of creative expression (e.g. performing art, cinema and literature)

Unit III: Traditional medium, materials and techniques and their application in all disciplines of visual expression (carving and casting processes; impasto, glazing; intaglio/relief print; fresco; preparation of ground for murals, wasli for miniatures)

Unit IV: Developments in modern techniques, processes and procedures and their application in contemporary visual practices (installation; multi-colour print; computer-aided design — vector and raster; multimedia and digital technologies in art; trompe l'oeil illusory hyper-realism)
Unit V: Indian and Western aesthetics and art appreciation
Unit VI: Chronological periods from prehistory to post-modern art and artists of the West, with a focus on the movements that transformed its history
Unit VII: Chronological periods and developments in Indian art from prehistory to the 19th century

Unit VIII: Contemporary practices in Indian art during the 20th and 21st centuries; modern concept of advertising, designing and visual communication; experimental modes in contemporary visual expression; development of art education in India from colonial art schools to the present
Unit IX: Art of the Far East, South East and Central Asia and the ancient Near-East
Unit X: Visual practices of traditional communities and their contemporary transformations — the folk, tribal and craft practices in India
Elective I: Art History
Elective II: Drawing and Painting
Elective III: Applied Art
Elective IV: Printmaking (Graphic Art)
Elective V: Sculpture

sources.nature: official (syllabus index page that lists the PDF links)

topics: Unit I (common to all in music): Technical Terms (sangeet, nada, shruti, swaras, raga, thata, tala, laya, gamaka, notation systems, etc.)

Unit II (common): Folk Music (origin, evolution and classification of Indian folk music; folk instruments and performers of various regions; ragas and talas used in folk music; folk fairs and festivals)

Unit III (common): Rasa and Aesthetics (rasa according to Bharata and others; rasa nishpatti and its application to Indian classical music; aesthetics according to Indian and western philosophers; raga-ragini paintings)
Unit IV (common): Research Methodology and Pedagogy, Avenues, Interdisciplinary aspects and Modern Technology

Hindustani (Vocal, Instrumental & Musicology) Unit V: Applied Theory (sangeet utpatti; musical scales Indian and western; gram, murchchhana; raga classification; time theory of ragas; notation systems of Hindustani, Karnataka and western music; layakari)
Hindustani Unit VI: History of Indian Music, contribution of Musicologists and their textual tradition
Hindustani Unit VII: Compositional forms and their evolution (prabandh, dhrupad, dhamaar, kheyaal, tarana, thumri, tappa etc.)
Hindustani Unit VIII: Musical Instruments and their Classification
Hindustani Unit IX: Contribution of composers/performers to Indian music (Tansen, Sadarang etc.)
Hindustani Unit X: Gharana and Institutional System and conferences of Hindustani music
Karnataka Music Unit V: Applied Theory (musical scales; suddha and vikrita svaras; sruti; raga-lakshana and classification; talas; notation and staff notation)
Karnataka Music Unit VI: Historical perspective of music — contributions of scholars, musicologists, musical concepts in treatises
Karnataka Music Unit VII: Compositional forms and their evolution (prabandha, gitam, svarajati, varnam, padavarnam, kriti, ragamalika etc.)
Karnataka Music Unit VIII: Music Instruments of India (classification, structure and playing techniques; veena, violin, flute, nadaswaram, mridangam etc.)
Karnataka Music Unit IX: Contribution of composers/performers to music, Indian and western (Tevaram, Alwars, Purandara Dasa, the music trinity etc.)
Karnataka Music Unit X: Prominent Banis, music training, education and propagation (gurukula sampradaya, institutional training)

Percussion (Tabla/Pakhawaj) Units V-X: Applied Theory — Taal & Avanaddha Vadya; history of music and treatises; compositional forms of avanaddha vadyas; classification and description of musical instruments; performers and composers; detailed study of gharanas and institutional system

Rabindra Sangeet Units V-X: Applied Theory (ragas, talas, kirtana, baul); historical perspective of music (Tagore and eminent personalities); composition forms and their evolution (Geetanjali and song offerings); music instruments of India; contribution of scholars/performers and their textual traditions; gharana and institutionalised system of music

topics: Paper 1 Listening — Section A: Compositional Techniques and Performance Practice (aural perception, music literacy and applied contextual understanding in relation to the set works)
Paper 1 Listening — Section B: Understanding Music (musical understanding, including compositional techniques and their effects, in the set works)
Paper 1 Listening — Section C: Connecting Music (wider knowledge of musical genres and styles beyond the set works)
Component 2 Practical Music — performing (6-10 minute performance)
Component 2 Practical Music — composing (two contrasting compositions, 1-2 minutes each)
Component 3 Extended Performance — 15-20 minute performance plus 1000-1500-word research report
Component 4 Extended Composition — 6-8 minute composition plus 1000-1500-word research report
Component 5 Investigating Music — 2500-3000-word essay plus up to 500-word reflective statement
Core musical activities across components: listening, composing and performing, working with Western notation and connecting a wide variety of music

sources.nature: official (ibo.org Cloudflare-blocked from this sandbox; URL known, content taken from the two mirrors)

topics: Comparative Study (CS) — analytical comparison of artworks by different artists from different cultural contexts, examining formal qualities, function, meaning and cultural significance; at HL also a connection to the student's own work
Process Portfolio (PP) — documentation of experimentation, skill-building, critical reflection and range of media across the course
Exhibition — a curated selection of resolved artworks with a curatorial rationale explaining choices and connections

SL (150 hours) and HL (240 hours) follow the same three assessed components, with HL requiring a larger Comparative Study with explicit link to own practice, more Process Portfolio screens covering more media, and a larger Exhibition with fuller rationale
